sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Lansing
sections.html:
Lansing splits the work among the City Assessor, the Treasury and Income Tax Office and the Board of Review. The assessor tracks and values every assessable property in the city each year. The treasury office collects the tax. The board hears valuation appeals under state law and city ordinance.

Geography adds a wrinkle. Most of Lansing sits in Ingham County, but parts reach into Eaton and Clinton counties, and the city's millage library lists levies from all three. The county named on your bill also decides which treasurer collects after a tax goes delinquent, so read that line before you phone anyone.

Lansing has 113,884 residents. Owners occupy 53.8% of homes, so about 46% are rented. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $128,700, median gross rent is $993, and median household income is $54,382.

At a $128,700 typical value, a fixed charge such as the $175 title search fee added at forfeiture takes a larger share of the bill than it would on a higher priced house.

sections.h2: Tax rates on a Lansing bill
sections.html:
The city's millage library posts every levy for the 2025 tax year. A mill is $1 of tax per $1,000 of taxable value. A parcel in the Lansing School District picks up city, county, school and college levies. These are the summer levies for a parcel in Ingham County and the Lansing School District:

Summer 2025 millage, Ingham County parcel in the Lansing School District
LevySummer 2025 mills
City of Lansing operating19.4400
City of Lansing public safety3.5000
Lansing School District operating17.4478
Lansing School District debt4.1000
Lansing School District sinking fund2.9468
State education tax6.0000
Lansing Community College3.7550
Ingham County operating6.7548

The intermediate school district, storm drains and other levies are in the library too. Use the library for the full set and your actual bill for the final figure. A homeowner with a principal residence exemption does not pay the school operating levy, which is the 17.4478 line.

sections.h2: How the county changes your bill
sections.html:
Eaton and Clinton parcels carry county, township and transit levies that an Ingham parcel never sees. The library separates them by county, which is why two Lansing neighbors on opposite sides of a county line can pay different totals.

  • Ingham County parcels show Ingham County operating at 6.7548 mills in summer and 5.6614 in winter.
  • Eaton County parcels add Eaton County operating at 5.2023 mills in summer, plus winter levies for the jail (0.6983), 911 (0.9486), roads (1.4964), parks (0.4993) and EATRAN (0.2493).
  • Clinton County parcels add Clinton County operating at 5.7288 mills in summer, with winter levies for DeWitt Township operating (3.9736), fire (1.2239), police (1.2239) and Clinton Transit (0.6962).

These are 2025 tax year rates from the city's library, and your own statement is the final word.

Tax unpaid on March 1 of the following year goes to the county treasurer with a 4% fee and 1% monthly interest (MCL 211.78a). Summer tax collected with city taxes carries interest after September 14 (MCL 211.44a).

  • City levies and Lansing School District levies are summer items. Ingham County operating appears on both the summer and winter bills.
  • A parcel returned delinquent can be forfeited, foreclosed and sold under MCL 211.78 to 79a.
  • Owners who want a notice when tax is returned on a parcel can pay the county treasurer up to $5 a year, by February 1.

The Ingham, Eaton or Clinton County treasurer takes the parcel depending on where it lies, and each runs its own payoff process. Request a figure for your exact closing date, since interest builds month by month.

The Treasury and Income Tax Office lists six ways to pay: ACH payments, a drop box or in person, mail, MSU Federal Credit Union, online, and by phone. The city's Ways to Pay Property Tax page has a tab for each method, and the treasury office can tell you where to drop a payment and what each channel costs.

If your lender escrows the taxes, confirm the lender has paid before September 14 and before the winter due date instead of assuming it did. Because the city operating and public safety levies, the school levies, the state education tax and Lansing Community College are all on the summer bill, September 14 is the date that matters for most of a Lansing owner's tax.

Take it to the Lansing Board of Review, which opens on the second Monday of March, or the Tuesday or Wednesday that week if the city has picked one of those. State law (MCL 211.30) requires 12 hours of sessions in the first week, at least three of them after 6 pm.

A resident can protest by letter only if the city has adopted a resolution allowing it, and the city must say so on its assessment notices. You should get a written decision by the first Monday in June with details on the Michigan Tax Tribunal. The July and December boards are mainly for qualified errors and reach back one year.

The principal residence exemption lifts the school operating levy off a home you own and occupy, which on an Ingham parcel in the Lansing School District is the 17.4478 mill line. That is the largest single item you can remove, so it is worth confirming it is on your record.

When you sell, ask the assessor how the exemption is rescinded on your side, and expect the buyer to file their own. Tell the closing agent the date you moved out so the final bills are split correctly.

sections.h2: Selling a Lansing house with taxes owed
sections.html:
Tax is cleared at closing and the buyer's value is reset. A deed with warranty covenants needs a treasurer's certificate of no liens and five paid years (MCL 211.135), so any delinquent balance, with its 4% fee and interest, comes out of the seller's proceeds.

MCL 211.27a then moves the taxable value to the state equalized value for the year after the transfer, and the buyer must tell the local assessor within 45 days. That reset can raise a parcel's bill after a sale.

Have your parcel number and latest bill ready when you ask the treasury for a payoff, since the county on the bill decides who answers. A seller with back tax who wants a fast, as-is sale should get the payoff first and then weigh it against any offer.

faqs.q: Which county collects delinquent tax on a Lansing house?
faqs.a: The county where the parcel lies. Lansing is mostly in Ingham County with sections in Eaton and Clinton counties, and the treasurer of that county collects what the city could not.

faqs.q: What is the Lansing city millage rate?
faqs.a: The 2025 millage library lists 19.4400 mills for city operating and 3.5000 mills for city public safety on the summer bill. Those are in addition to school, county and college levies, and your own bill is the final word.

faqs.q: When is the Lansing Board of Review?
faqs.a: The second Monday in March, with Tuesday or Wednesday that week allowed if the city chooses. A July or December board handles clerical and similar errors.

faqs.q: Does Lansing add penalties to late property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Summer tax collected after September 14 picks up interest, and a March 1 return to the county adds a 4% fee plus 1% interest per month.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lansing house that owes back property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance is subtracted from your proceeds at closing, and the county treasurer's certificate of five paid years is needed for a warranty deed. Request the payoff before choosing a closing date.
